title: Make It Think + Your Midterm
subtitle: Monday: the same loop, the same tools, one paragraph — and your agent plans before it acts. Wednesday: one agent or many, what MCP actually is, and the midterm project assigned with a plan on paper before you leave.
heroTitle: Make It Think

objectives.title: Turn a Lookup Bot into a Researcher
objectives.description: ReAct: think, act, observe, repeat. One paragraph of system prompt, zero changes to the loop. Run the same question at three levels and read the agent's thoughts.

objectives.title: Price the Thinking
objectives.description: Steps, tool calls, thinking tokens, dollars. ReAct is several times more expensive than a plain loop, so deciding which questions deserve it is a business decision you can now make with numbers.

objectives.title: Decide One Agent or Many
objectives.description: Pipeline, orchestrator, debate, and the rule that more agents is not more intelligence. Split only for a reason you can name: permissions, specialization, context isolation, parallelism. Plus MCP, and why a protocol is not a permission.

objectives.title: Start Your Midterm with a Plan
objectives.description: Your bot, for a real problem: one user, two tools with one real API, the trust layer, five tests, one honest page. Assigned Wednesday, kicked off on paper in class, due Mon Nov 2.

agenda.title: Meeting 1 · HW #7 Pulse + The Pattern Gap
agenda.description: Which vendor said 'not disclosed'? Then: your bot answers the first thing it can, and a researcher plans first.
bulletPoints: Three levels of the same agent: the model alone, your Session 4 loop, ReAct
The paragraph: THINK before every call, OBSERVE after, and never invent when a tool says 'no results'
Nobody touched the loop. The loop can't tell the difference. The model can

agenda.title: Live, Then Hands-On: Same Question, Three Times
agenda.description: 'How is AI affecting employment?' at levels 0, 1, and 2 on the projector, then on your own key. Count the hops, read the thoughts, run the bill.
bulletPoints: Only your Gemini key today — tools are calculator, the job board, and real Wikipedia
The bill table: steps, tool calls, thinking tokens, dollars — how many times more did thinking cost?
Stop at Part 5; we break it together

agenda.title: Part 5 Together: When Does It Fail?
agenda.description: A company that does not exist, an opinion dressed as research, and a calculator question with ReAct on.
bulletPoints: QuantumLeaf Technologies: does it admit there is no data, or produce a revenue figure?
The fix for a confident fake is a sentence in the tool description, not a bigger model
Part 6: one line puts the paragraph in your phone bot, one more line routes simple lookups around it

agenda.title: Wrap: Boardroom + Wednesday
agenda.description: Why the vendor's agent takes 20 seconds, whether it can show its work, and what to bring Wednesday.
bulletPoints: HW #7 due Thu Oct 22, 11:59 PM
Wednesday: one agent or many, MCP, and the midterm assigned — bring one real problem and the name of one person who has it

agenda.title: Meeting 2 · One Agent or Many?
agenda.description: Three patterns on paper, the rule for splitting, your phone bot as the case, and MCP in one slide.
bulletPoints: Pipeline, orchestrator, debate — every box is the Session 4 loop; multi-agent is an org chart
Split only when you can name the reason: permissions, specialization, context isolation, parallelism
Pair exercise: should your phone bot become two? The first legitimate split is permissions, the day send_email talks to a real inbox
MCP: a standard plug for tools. A protocol is not a permission

agenda.title: The Midterm Project, Assigned
agenda.description: Your bot, for a real problem. Four requirements, the rubric, the bonuses, the grad addendum. Due Mon Nov 2, 12:30 PM.
bulletPoints: One real problem, one named user, two tools with one real API, the trust layer, five tests (two hostile), a one-page memo
Individual. Colab notebook with outputs + memo PDF on Canvas. 20% of the grade (ISOM 900: 15% plus an architecture page)

agenda.title: Kickoff: Leave with a Plan
agenda.description: Ten minutes alone on paper, eight minutes of a neighbor trying to break it, three volunteers and a room vote.
bulletPoints: The sheet: problem · user's name · two tools (which API?) · the risky action and who approves · five queries, two hostile
Neighbor's three questions: would a stranger use this? what's the API? what breaks?
Photograph the sheet. It is the first draft of your memo

activities.discussionNote: The plan is where midterms are won. Code is the easy part now.

takeaways.text: Reasoning is a paragraph, not a model upgrade. Think, act, observe, repeat. The loop never changed; the behavior did.
Thinking has a price. ReAct costs several times a plain loop. Route research to it and lookups around it. That routing is a business decision.
The fix for a confident fake is in the tool. A tool that says 'no results' plus a prompt that forbids filling the gap. You wrote both.
More agents is not more intelligence. Start with one. Split only for a reason you can name: permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism.
A protocol is not a permission. MCP standardizes the plug. It does not open the door.
